entries.title: Games: Sudoku, Snake, 2048, Minesweeper and Spin the wheel
entries.text: Four classics and a fair prize wheel, built for a phone and a keyboard: swipe and tap controls, saved games and best scores, light and dark mode. Each game has its own music, generated live in the browser, and sound effects you can turn off. Spin the wheel lets you choose the elements and odds, then spin it full screen or print a poster with every probability.
entries.tools: JavaScript, canvas, Web Audio, game design

entries.title: Taylor rule for Norges Bank
entries.text: What a simple Taylor rule says Norway’s policy rate should be, against what Norges Bank actually set since 2015, with data from Norges Bank and Statistics Norway. An AI agent updates it twice a month.
entries.tools: Monetary policy, Hodrick-Prescott filter, Python, JavaScript

entries.title: Bonds and the yield curve
entries.text: The Norwegian government yield curve from Norges Bank’s daily data, and a calculator for price, duration, convexity and what a rate shock does to a bond.

entries.title: Option pricing
entries.text: Black–Scholes and binomial pricing side by side, with the Greeks, early exercise for American options and a check against the textbook examples.

entries.title: LBO calculator
entries.text: A leveraged buyout of a fictional company: set the price, the debt and the plan, and see the IRR, the money multiple, where the gain comes from and how sensitive it is to the exit price.

entries.title: Case interview trainer
entries.text: Five practice cases with a timer, exhibits, answer checks and model answers, from market sizing to profitability and investment cases, plus a mental maths drill.

entries.title: How I work with AI agents
entries.text: The scheduled agents behind this site and my working day, the rules that check their output, and four times they got it wrong.

entries.title: Market analysis: Norwegian grocery retail
entries.text: Three groups sell almost all groceries in Norway and low-price chains keep growing. The change to watch is the government’s plan to open the big groups’ wholesale systems to small challengers. The first in a weekly series with competitor analysis, PESTEL and SWOT.
entries.tools: Market analysis, competitor analysis, PESTEL, SWOT

entries.title: CV builder
entries.text: Upload a CV as PDF or Word, or start from scratch, and download a clean one-page version as a Word file or PDF. The text scales to fit one page, and a writing check flags bullet points without numbers or with weak verbs.

entries.title: What does Gjensidige’s share price assume?
entries.text: A justified price-to-book valuation that works backwards from the share price to the return on equity the market is pricing in.

entries.title: Who makes money on insurance itself?
entries.text: Combined ratios for Gjensidige, Tryg and Sampo since 2023, and what drives the differences between them.

entries.title: Simulating a year of claims
entries.text: A Monte Carlo simulation of an insurer’s annual claims that shows how often premiums fall short and how much capital the worst year in 200 requires. Also written in Python. Now with a deductible per claim and a note on how Norsk Naturskadepool shares storm losses in Norway.
entries.tools: Monte Carlo simulation, Solvency II, JavaScript, Python

entries.title: Portfolio and CAPM calculator
entries.text: An interactive efficient frontier for two assets, the best risk-adjusted mix and the required return on equity.

entries.title: Case: student contents insurance
entries.text: A consulting-style case that sizes the market for contents insurance among students in Norway, tests the assumptions and recommends how an insurer should approach the segment.

entries.title: Careless or grossly careless?
entries.text: How Norwegian insurance law separates ordinary carelessness from gross negligence, explained through two cases from the complaints board.

entries.title: What does it cost to wait?
entries.text: A conceptual study of how to prioritise tasks. The result is an index that ranks tasks by cost of delay per calibrated hour, with urgency calculated from the slack to each deadline, plus a check that shows overload before it becomes a crisis. Built as a calculator too.
entries.tools: Scheduling theory, decision analysis, behavioural economics, JavaScript

entries.title: Market concentration calculator
entries.text: Calculates the Herfindahl–Hirschman Index for any market and shows what a merger would do to concentration. Comes loaded with the Norwegian non-life insurance market.

entries.title: Young adults and insurance loyalty
entries.text: Group project in Methods and Insight at BI: a market study of what drives loyalty among 18–29-year-olds in Norway, with If P&C Insurance as the case. Three focus groups, 187 survey respondents and four customer segments from cluster analysis.
entries.tools: JMP, focus groups, cluster analysis, ANOVA, regression

entries.title: Overtime pay for part-time staff
entries.text: A legal opinion, written in Norwegian, on whether part-time employees can claim back overtime pay for hours worked beyond their contract. It covers the EU case law, the two district court judgments from 2026, both sides’ arguments, limitation periods and cost, and ends with a likely conclusion. Includes a calculator for the claim.
entries.tools: Employment law, EEA law, arbeidsmiljøloven, foreldelsesloven, JavaScript

entries.title: Learning to use AI proficiently
entries.text: A guide to using AI as an employee you train rather than a slot machine, built on a Dan Koe podcast episode. It covers teaching the AI a task, metaprompts, prompt libraries and AI as a thinking partner, then applies the method to market analysis. Includes figures, prompt templates and a prompt builder.
entries.tools: Prompt engineering, metaprompts, market analysis, JavaScript
